# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Thursday, November 26, 2026

Thursday edition for 26 November 2026 (IST), covering Wednesday 25 November to Thursday morning; data compiled 07:01–07:40 IST. Today is a normal trading day — the NSE holiday master puts the next equity-segment holiday at 25 December 2026, with nothing between — so the market opens at 09:15 as usual. **Every index and stock figure below is Wednesday 25 November's close**, from the NSE's own files for the date; the Sensex is a BSE index and is cited to BusinessLine, never to the NSE archive. IBJA's block this morning still reads "Rates will be uploaded soon" — a normal session not yet posted at the 07:03 read, not a holiday state — so the domestic benchmark below is the **25 November PM session, labelled as such**. **AGLOC's block is available and dated 26 November 2026, and unlike yesterday's it is a fresh move**: its reference is the 25 November PM 916 rate, not a print carried over the holiday. Thursday is a two-report day — news and regulation; the weekly analysis desk files on Mondays, and the 23 November Monday edition stands on the record as published with that desk missing (2 of 3), which this edition flags and does not repair.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### Margin calls have started: banks and NBFCs are asking gold-loan borrowers for more collateral or part-repayment
The report that changes the shape of this story landed in Mint on 25 November at 11:55 IST: "Sharp drop in gold prices triggers margin calls on loans by banks and NBFCs — what customers should know about LTV", by Bobins Vayalil Abraham. **Banks and NBFCs have accelerated sending notices and reminders to customers, asking them to provide additional security or repay a part of their gold loan, because the pledged gold no longer covers the RBI LTV limit.** Everything before this in the cycle was warning and monitoring — the RBI's 23 November meeting with NBFC, HFC and microfinance chief executives in Mumbai (readout, press release 2026-2027/1554), the reported increase in portfolio-reporting frequency, the caution that LTVs skew as prices fall. **This is the first report in this cycle that borrowers are actually being asked for more collateral, not merely warned.**

The credit data behind the asking is TransUnion CIBIL's, as cited in the same piece: **gold-loan NPAs stood at 0.30% at end-August 2026, up from 0.16% at 31 March 2026**, and borrowers with multiple gold-loan accounts are more prone to delay. The piece's own market read puts 24K gold hovering between ₹12,458 and ₹12,632 a gram on 25 November, with prices fallen roughly 30% to 35% from their January 2026 record highs — Mint's quote of the retail market, not an IBJA print, and kept apart from the benchmark figures below.

Two named industry voices carry the lender side, each attributed to the person and the outlet. **Mayank Sharma, president-lending at IIFL Finance, told PTI** the industry "could see a significant increase in gold auctions this year once prices stabilise over a longer period", and: "At the current gold price, there will be a greater focus on customer collections and interest collections." **Pinaki Nath Banerjee, CEO-designate of the Federation of Gold Loan Companies (FGLOC)**, said repayment challenges have emerged after the correction — and that fresh loan demand remains healthy; the industry is unlikely to match its prior growth, because rising prices had inflated collateral values. IIFL Finance is a listed gold-loan peer and FGLOC is the industry's federation; **neither voice speaks for Muthoot Fincorp**, and the CIBIL figure is an industry-level metric, not any single lender's book. Muthoot Finance is a separate listed company, and no statement in this report belongs to it unless attributed to it.

The piece restates the RBI's standing LTV bands — **85% for loans up to ₹2.5 lakh, 80% for ₹2.5–5 lakh, 75% above ₹5 lakh** — the structure under which such notices go out. No RBI instrument dated 24, 25 or 26 November changes them, and the rules report today records that no instrument of any regulator changes a rule applying to Muthoot Fincorp's lending business.

What was already on the record, each item with its own date and none of it today's news: the Economic Times reported on 24 November at 01:11 IST that the RBI told NBFCs at the 23 November meeting to scrutinise gold-loan LTVs as prices fall, and that the ₹10-crore net owned fund threshold arrives by March 2027 with no further extension; Moneycontrol reported on 23 November at 10:04 IST that the RBI has raised the frequency of portfolio reporting over the last 30–45 days, that some loans stand above 100% LTV, and that gold loans stood at **₹3.74 trillion in September 2026, up 66.1% year-on-year**; and Crisil, via Business Today on 24 November, expects gold-loan AUM growth to moderate to about **40% in FY27 from 78% in FY26** and does not anticipate a significant rise in credit costs.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the mechanism Mint describes — notices, additional security, part-repayment, auctions — is the same ongoing-LTV maintenance that applies across gold-loan lenders, including Muthoot Fincorp. No public document states how many such notices the company has sent or where its book sits against the bands, and no such figure is asserted here.

### The 25 November session: the market rallied and gold-loan names sat it out
The market reopened on Wednesday after Tuesday's Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday and rallied hard. The **Nifty 50 closed at 25,819.25, up 469.60 points or 1.85%**; **Nifty Bank 63,703.25, up 1,117.90 or 1.79%**; **Nifty Financial Services 28,764.95, up 611.45 or 2.17%**; Nifty Midcap 100 61,584.75, up 0.30%; Nifty Smallcap 100 19,229.35, down 0.44%; India VIX 17.67, off 0.16%. The **Sensex — a BSE index, not in the NSE archive — closed at 83,938.28, up 1,502.29 points or 1.82%** (BusinessLine's 25 November closing bell, 16:15 IST).

The useful read is the divergence inside the rally. Financials led — Financial Services +2.17%, Bank +1.79% — but **Nifty NBFC rose only 1.22%, to 56,327.67**, and the listed gold-loan names lagged far worse: **Muthoot Finance +0.25% at ₹2,549.60; Manappuram −1.29% at ₹267.50; IIFL Finance −0.73% at ₹610.50; Shriram Finance −0.60% at ₹989.95; Muthoot Microfin −0.76% at ₹158.85 — while Bajaj Finance rose 3.27% to ₹1,131.35.** On a day the Nifty rose 1.85% and financials 2.17%, the gold-loan peers underperformed the financial rally even as the Sensex gained 1,502 points. **Muthoot Finance is a listed peer, not Muthoot Fincorp; Muthoot Microfin is a listed group company, not Muthoot Fincorp either; and every price above belongs to the company whose ticker printed it.**

The currency moved the other way: the **rupee strengthened 0.7% to 92.23 against the dollar, an eight-month high, with an intraday print at 92.1850** (BusinessLine). FMCG led sectoral gains, metal and media lagged, and Brent eased to around $90.10 a barrel — an indication from the session wrap, not a settlement.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none directly. Muthoot Fincorp is unlisted and has no share price in either index, and the divergence is a comparison of index and ticker moves, not evidence about any single lender's book.

### Gold falls a second straight session; the deferred domestic re-pricing lands, and AGLOC's block moves for real
Comex front-month gold — November delivery, a settlement, not spot — **settled at $3,534.70 an ounce on Wednesday 25 November, down $25.20 or 0.71% on the prior settlement of $3,559.90, a second consecutive decline**; the prior print had itself been described by Dow Jones as the second-lowest of the year, and the dollar change here is arithmetic on the two documented settles rather than a figure the 25 November report states. No source in this pack calls Wednesday's print the lowest of the year; what is on the record is that it is lower again than a print so described (Dow Jones Market Data, 25 Nov; prior settle and the "second-lowest" description from Dow Jones's 24 November Data Talk). Reuters, in the same day's reporting, had US gold futures for December delivery down 0.73% to $3,535.8 — a different contract on a different clock, kept apart here; the settlements in this report are front-month November-delivery prints, not spot, not MCX, not IBJA.

Silver fell harder, and its record-keeping is specific: Comex front-month **settled at $40.052 an ounce, down 70.80 cents or 1.74% — a new 52-week low and the lowest settlement since 28 August 2025**; down two consecutive sessions and **$3.095 or 7.17% over the two, the largest two-day dollar and percentage decline since 20 November**; down eight of the past 10 sessions; **65.20% below the 52-week and record high of $115.08** set on 26 January; month-to-date −18.42% and year-to-date −42.89% (Dow Jones Data Talk, 25 Nov, 13:54 ET).

The domestic benchmark took the deferred move in one print. IBJA's **25 November PM session — the latest posted, because this morning's block still reads "Rates will be uploaded soon", a normal session not yet posted at the 07:03 IST read — put 999 at ₹1,21,038 per 10 g (₹12,103.8 a gram) and 916 at ₹1,10,871 (₹11,087.1 a gram)**, against 23 November PM closes of ₹1,24,945 and ₹1,14,450: **−₹3,907 (−3.13%) on 999 and −₹3,579 (−3.13%) on 916 — the re-pricing the 24 November holiday had deferred.** Silver 999 fell ₹9,680 (−6.34%) to ₹1,42,945 a kg. Within the day, the PM session sat ₹272 below the AM on 999 and ₹249 below on 916. Week-to-date on the 916 PM series: ₹1,13,486 on 20 November, ₹1,14,450 on 23 November (+0.85%), ₹1,10,871 on 25 November (−3.13%) — the 20 November print had been the low of this cycle until Wednesday's session took it out.

**AGLOC's block is dated 26 November 2026, was read today, and is a fresh move, not a carry-forward**: ₹9,424 a gram at 85% LTV, ₹8,869 at 80% and ₹8,315 at 75%, **on a jewellery reference of ₹11,087 — which is IBJA's 25 November PM 916 rate ÷ 10**, where yesterday's block had rested on the 23 November PM rate carried over the holiday. Against the 25 November block (₹9,728 / ₹9,156 / ₹8,583 on ₹11,445), the changes are **−₹304 at the 85% band, −₹287 at 80% and −₹268 at 75%, with the reference down ₹358**; the percentages are arithmetic on AGLOC's own two blocks, as the page states rupee figures only. **All three bands move together because they are fixed percentages of the one reference — one observation, not three.**

On the domestic exchange, the 25 November session closed the December contracts lower: **MCX GOLD 04DEC2026 at ₹1,21,137 per 10 g, down ₹1,192 or 0.97%, and MCX SILVER 04DEC2026 at ₹1,42,517 a kg, down ₹2,921 or 2.01%** — quote-board prices, not exchange settlements, and no rupee change is derived from them for any other contract. Gold swung ₹4,214 inside the day — open 1,21,900, high 1,22,120, low 1,17,906 — and closed almost flat-to-down; silver ran from 1,45,386 down to 1,36,712. The timing is worth stating: IBJA's Wednesday print was struck in the afternoon IST, and Comex's Wednesday settlements were fixed in New York after the US close — the silver Data Talk carries a 13:54 ET timestamp and the gold series publishes at 18:52 GMT (6:52 PM ET), the same clock the 23 and 24 November gold Data Talks carry — so the domestic print and the Comex settlement measure different windows of the same fall.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the operative AGLOC ceiling for today is ₹9,424 at the 85% band, ₹304 below yesterday's — the first fresh move in the published ceiling since the holiday, and it is downward. The ceiling applies across lenders; no Muthoot Fincorp-specific figure is in any public document, and none is inferred.

### The macro driver: October PCE at 3.8%, Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%, and markets fully price a December hike
The backdrop to the metals move and the rupee, reported as reported and asserted as nothing more: **US October PCE inflation came in at +0.3% month-on-month and 3.8% year-on-year, up from 3.7% in September; core +0.3% m/m and 3.3% y/y, up from 3.1% and above a 3.2% forecast** (CNBC's live blog of the 25 November session, whose running copy carries the PCE release and the core reading; the metals wire story separately reports the headline +0.3% m/m). **Third-quarter GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualised from 3.4%, against a consensus of 3.5%** (the same session coverage). **Markets fully price a December Fed hike, per CME FedWatch as cited in the same reporting** — a market price, not a Fed announcement, and this report writes it as one. New US tariff proposals on major trading partners are also cited in the same reporting.

The US equity close on 25 November: the **Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 164.25 (0.33%) to 50,182.95**; the **S&P 500 fell 18.31 (0.25%) to 7,182.78**; the **Nasdaq Composite fell 147.73 (0.62%) to 23,585.80** (AP's index wrap). The Dow erased an intraday loss of more than 1,100 points and the Nasdaq was down 4.6% at its low (CNBC's live coverage of the session); AI-linked stocks fell for a second day after Monday's Nvidia-driven relief rally — all as reported, none of it a forecast adopted here.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none directly. US policy pricing moves the dollar, the metals and the rupee, which set the collateral arithmetic above; nothing here is a prediction of the Fed's December decision.

## 🏛️ RBI & Regulatory — Headlines Only

### SEBI's two 25 November circulars are new; neither binds an NBFC as a lender, and the RBI's lists have not moved
**No RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument dated 24, 25 or 26 November changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp's lending business.** The RBI's press-release list, read to its 25 November block, carries only liquidity operations and reports on it — an Overnight Variable Rate Repo auction under LAF for 26 November, the 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves (April–September 2026), the November 2026 RBI Bulletin, and T-Bill and VRR auction results — with nothing dated 26 November at the 07:03 read, which came before the day's postings. The notifications list still stands at its 23 November block of four parallel securitisation amendments; the NBFC one takes effect 1 April 2027 and was covered in the 23 November edition. The RBI has changed no rule on any day covered here.

SEBI's two 25 November circulars are new since yesterday's edition, and both are real instruments; **neither is addressed to an NBFC as a lender.** The half-yearly review of 'Significant Indices' under the SEBI (Index Providers) Regulations, 2024 — circular HO/47/17/12(53)2026-MRD-POD5/I/26407/2026 — reviewed the six months to 30 June 2026 and **leaves the Annexure-A list unchanged**: BSE 200 and Nifty CPSE, which did not meet the ₹20,000-crore AUM-tracking threshold, are retained under Para 5 of the May 2026 circular. It is effective immediately and binds **index providers, stock exchanges, mutual funds, AMCs and AMFI** — it changes nothing on the list, and it does not reach Muthoot Fincorp's gold-loan business.

The second — the simplification of client on-boarding and rationalisation of risk management at KYC Registration Agencies, HO/38/14/(25)2026-MIRSD-POD3 — amends the October 2023 KYC Master Circular: it centralises supplementary client information at KRA level, adds CKYC ID, DIGIPIN and OVD expiry date to the upload set, requires intermediaries to upload within three working days of completing KYC, and **takes effect 24 December 2026**. Its scope is **intermediaries registered under Section 12 of the SEBI Act, recognised stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories**. **A gold-loan NBFC is not a Section 12 intermediary unless separately registered — for example as a depository participant — and this circular does not bind Muthoot Fincorp's lending business**; its relevance runs to group or affiliate entities that are SEBI-registered intermediaries, and to KYC data quality generally. IBBI was checked with no update date assertable from the page as read.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none today. The operative rulebook — the RBI's gold-loan LTV framework — is unchanged, and both circulars' scopes stop short of NBFC lending.

## 🏢 Muthoot Fincorp in the market

### The investor page re-read: 873 documents, unchanged; the EGM papers are named and still unreadable
Muthoot Fincorp's investor page was re-read through the gated route at 07:02 IST and shows **no new filing seen**: **873 distinct document names — deduplicated on the S3 basenames across the banner's presigned URLs — exactly as on 25 November**. The capture is **the same length as yesterday's — 2,770,369 bytes both days — and carries an identical set of document names, with none added and none removed**; the bytes are not identical, because the page rebuilds its presigned signatures and per-request script ids on every load, which is why the name set and not a hash is the signal that matters. The count is quoted as 873, unchanged; "no new filing seen" is the honest phrasing rather than "nothing was filed", because the announcements list is partly loaded by script and an item could still post later in the day.

The EGM trail is still on the page — **"Proceedings_of_the_EGM_held_on_November_23,_2026.pdf" and the intimation of the EGM** — and the two documents remain unreadable from here: their presigned links carry a 900-second expiry fixed at page-build time, and they have expired. **This edition reports that the documents exist, with their names and dates, and nothing more: what the meeting resolved is not readable from this fetch, and no outcome is inferred.** An EGM's business could be borrowing limits, preference-share conversion, director appointments or the IPO; guessing which would be fabrication, and none is attempted.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none asserted. The proceedings document is the authority on what the EGM resolved; until it is readable, the meeting is recorded here only as held, with its papers posted and unreadable.
Sources: [Muthoot Fincorp investor page, re-read 26 Nov 07:02 IST](https://www.muthootfincorp.com/investors)

### Muthoot Microfin's postal ballot on related-party transactions with the parent runs to 13 December
The standing group item, unchanged today: Muthoot Microfin's postal ballot on material related party transactions with Muthoot Fincorp — **up to ₹2,500 crore, including gold-loan assignments and co-lending** — has remote e-voting open from **14 November to 13 December 2026**, with results to be published **on or before 15 December 2026**. It is a shareholder approval of a transaction framework, not a new transaction; **Muthoot Microfin is the listed subsidiary, and the parent is the related party in it, not the filer** — a different company from Muthoot Fincorp, and from Muthoot Finance.

The subsidiary's shares last closed at **₹158.85 on 25 November, down ₹1.21 or 0.76%** (NSE bhavcopy).

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the ballot governs the assignment and co-lending arrangements the two companies use; the result is not known from here and is not predicted, and the e-voting window runs to 13 December.

### What a fresh reference does: the ceiling falls with the price, and the notices follow
The collateral arithmetic is one line: **the LTV bands are fixed percentages of a reference price, so when the reference falls 3.13% in one print, the permissible loan value per gram falls with it — ₹304 at the 85% band, ₹287 at 80%, ₹268 at 75% — on every ticket size at once.** A loan written against a higher reference then sits above its band until the borrower adds security or repays part of it, which is exactly what Mint reported lenders asking for on 25 November, under the RBI's standing bands — 85% up to ₹2.5 lakh, 80% for ₹2.5–5 lakh, 75% above ₹5 lakh.

reports.content:
# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Thursday, 26 November 2026 (IST)

Thursday edition for 26 November 2026 (IST), covering Wednesday 25 November to Thursday morning; regulator pages read 07:03–07:12 IST. **No new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument dated 24, 25 or 26 November changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp's lending business.** Two SEBI circulars dated 25 November are new since yesterday's edition — both are real instruments, and neither is addressed to an NBFC as a lender: one is the half-yearly review of 'Significant Indices', which changes nothing on the list it reviews, and the other simplifies client on-boarding at KYC Registration Agencies, binding Section 12 intermediaries, exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories from 24 December 2026. The RBI's press-release list, read to its 25 November block, carries only liquidity operations and reports; its notifications list still stands at the 23 November block of four parallel securitisation amendments, the NBFC one effective 1 April 2027. What follows: the two circulars scoped plainly, the standing LTV bands with AGLOC's fresh 26 November block, what was checked, the latest circulars list, and the open deadlines.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

The one-line position: **nothing new binds the company today.** The two new SEBI instruments are scoped to index providers and to market intermediaries; the RBI has changed no rule on any day covered here — its newest notification block is still 23 November — and IBBI was checked with no date assertable. Both circulars are described below by their own scope, and neither is presented as reaching Muthoot Fincorp's gold-loan business.

### SEBI: half-yearly review of 'Significant Indices' — the Annexure-A list is unchanged
SEBI issued circular **HO/47/17/12(53)2026-MRD-POD5/I/26407/2026 on 25 November 2026**, the half-yearly review of 'Significant Indices' under the SEBI (Index Providers) Regulations, 2024. An index comes under the review when the daily average cumulative AUM tracking it across mutual fund schemes exceeds **₹20,000 crore for each of the past six months**, measured to the half-year ends of 30 June and 31 December. For the review period **1 January to 30 June 2026, the Annexure-A list is unchanged**; two indices — **BSE 200 (Sr. No. 2) and Nifty CPSE (Sr. No. 33)** — did not meet the threshold but are **retained under Para 5 of the May 2026 circular**. The circular is **effective immediately**, and its scope is **index providers, stock exchanges, mutual funds, AMCs and AMFI**.

**It is not an NBFC instrument, and it changes nothing on the list it reviews.** Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none — the company is not an index provider, an exchange, a mutual fund or an AMC, and nothing in the circular addresses NBFC lending.
Sources: [SEBI circular, 25 Nov 2026](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/half-yearly-review-of-significant-indices-under-sebi-index-providers-regulations-2024_105853.html)

### SEBI: simplification of client on-boarding at KYC Registration Agencies — binds Section 12 intermediaries, in force 24 December 2026
SEBI issued circular **HO/38/14/(25)2026-MIRSD-POD3 on 25 November 2026** — "Simplification of client on-boarding and rationalisation of risk management framework at KYC Registration Agencies" — amending the KYC Master Circular (SEBI/HO/MIRSD/SECFATF/P/CIR/2023/169, 12 October 2023). It **centralises supplementary client information at KRA level**: the Part II account-opening-form data that is common across intermediaries, plus **CKYC ID, DIGIPIN — a 10-character geo-coded postal address — and OVD expiry date**. Intermediaries must upload Part I plus the Part II items — income range, FATCA/CRS, PEP status, occupation, CKYC ID, DIGIPIN and OVD expiry — **within three working days of completing KYC**. KRAs are to **tag validated and unvalidated records attribute-wise**, and intermediaries must seek additional information where a fetched record is unvalidated. The changes also apply to **individual Person Resident Outside India (PROI) clients from FATF-compliant countries** (paras 3.1–3.4, 3.6 and 3.7). **The circular comes into force on 24 December 2026** — thirty days from issue — and KRAs are to issue an SOP within the same 30 days.

Its scope is explicit: **intermediaries registered under Section 12 of the SEBI Act, recognised stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories. It is not addressed to NBFCs as lenders.** A gold-loan NBFC is not a Section 12 intermediary unless separately registered — for example as a depository participant — so this circular does not bind Muthoot Fincorp's lending business; its relevance runs to group or affiliate entities that are SEBI-registered intermediaries, and to KYC data quality generally. Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none on the lending business; the company's KYC obligations as an NBFC arise from the RBI's framework, not from this circular.
Sources: [SEBI circular, 25 Nov 2026](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/simplification-of-client-on-boarding-and-rationalisation-of-risk-management-framework-at-kyc-registration-agencies_105839.html)

### The next scheduled decision: the MPC meets 2–4 December
The Monetary Policy Committee's next meeting runs **2–4 December 2026, with the decision due on 4 December** — carried from the 25 November edition; no new schedule was read today, and nothing in today's pack adds to the policy position beyond the date, so nothing else is restated here.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the meeting sets the policy rate that floors the company's cost of funds; the outcome is not known from here and is not predicted.
Sources: [RBI press releases](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx)

## 📖 The standing rulebook: the LTV bands, unchanged; AGLOC's 26 November block is a fresh move
The gold-loan LTV bands that today's margin-call reporting restates are the standing ones: **85% for loans up to ₹2.5 lakh, 80% for loans between ₹2.5 and 5 lakh, 75% above ₹5 lakh**, as set out in Mint's 25 November report of the notices going out under them. **No RBI instrument dated 24, 25 or 26 November changes them, and no instrument of any regulator dated those days changes any other rule applying to Muthoot Fincorp's lending business.** AGLOC's block dated **26 November 2026** publishes the operative bands per gram — **₹9,424 at 85%, ₹8,869 at 80%, ₹8,315 at 75%, on a jewellery reference of ₹11,087** — and, unlike the 25 November block, it rests on a fresh reference: ₹11,087 is IBJA's 25 November PM 916 rate ÷ 10, not the 23 November print carried over the holiday. The changes from the previous block are **−₹304 at 85%, −₹287 at 80% and −₹268 at 75%, with the reference down ₹358**; the three bands move together because they are fixed percentages of the one reference — one observation, not three — and the percentages are arithmetic on AGLOC's own two blocks, not figures the page states.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: these bands and this reference govern the ceiling the company lends under; nothing in them changed today, and the fresh reference is a market print, not a rule move.
Sources: [Mint, 25 Nov 11:55 IST](https://www.livemint.com/money/personal-finance/sharp-drop-in-gold-prices-triggers-margin-calls-on-loans-by-banks-and-nbfcs-what-customers-should-know-about-ltv-11795587073208.html) · [AGLOC, block dated 26 Nov 2026](https://www.agloc.org/) · [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/)

## What was checked

The RBI's press-release listing was read at 07:03 IST on 26 November (HTTP 200, 161,289 bytes) and its newest block is dated 25 November 2026, whose newest item is an Overnight Variable Rate Repo auction under LAF for 26 November — a liquidity operation, not a rule; the other items on that block are the 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves (April–September 2026), the November 2026 RBI Bulletin, T-Bill auction results and VRR auction results, and nothing dated 26 November had posted at the read, which came before the day's postings; the 23 November block below it carries the Governor's meeting with the Managing Directors and CEOs of select NBFCs, HFCs and industry representatives in Mumbai on 23 November (readout 2026-2027/1554) and the Reserve Bank (Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026. The RBI's notifications listing, read at 07:03 IST (HTTP 200, 124,920 bytes), still carries its newest block at 23 November 2026 — four parallel instruments filed the same day, the securitisation amendment directions for All India Financial Institutions, for Non-Banking Financial Companies, for Small Finance Banks and for Commercial Banks — with nothing dated 24, 25 or 26 November above them; the NBFC instrument was already covered in the 23 November edition and takes effect 1 April 2027, and a note on reading them: four near-identical instruments filed by lender class invite the error of reading one and concluding it does not apply — for an NBFC, the NBFC one is the operative text. SEBI's circulars listing was read at 07:03 and again at 07:12 IST (HTTP 200, 45,839 bytes) and carries two circulars dated 25 November 2026, both new since yesterday's edition and both scoped above — the Significant Indices review, effective immediately, and the KRA on-boarding circular, in force 24 December 2026. IBBI's homepage was read at 07:03 IST (HTTP 200, 1,611,183 bytes) and carries no update date that can be asserted from the page as read, so none is asserted — checked, no date assertable — and no new insolvency instrument dated 24, 25 or 26 November was seen. The RBI's draft Amendment Directions on "Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions", carried from earlier editions, remain a draft for comment with feedback due 14 December 2026, scoped to banks and co-operative banks — a representation or a draft is not a rule change, and nothing in it binds an NBFC.
Sources: [RBI press releases](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx) · [RBI notifications](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx) · [SEBI: Significant Indices review, 25 Nov](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/half-yearly-review-of-significant-indices-under-sebi-index-providers-regulations-2024_105853.html) · [SEBI: KRA on-boarding circular, 25 Nov](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/simplification-of-client-on-boarding-and-rationalisation-of-risk-management-framework-at-kyc-registration-agencies_105839.html) · [SEBI circulars listing](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?doListing=yes&sid=1&ssid=7&smid=0) · [IBBI](https://ibbi.gov.in/)

latest_circulars.summary: The RBI published the 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks on 23 November 2026 (press release 2026-2027/1547). SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank remain D-SIBs under the same bucketing as 2025 : SBI in bucket 4 with 0.80% additional CET1 , HDFC Bank in bucket 2 with 0.40% , and ICICI Bank in bucket 1 with 0.20% .
latest_circulars.impact: none. A D-SIB surcharge is a bank capital requirement; the company's capital position is governed by the NBFC scale-based framework and its own reported CRAR of 19.38% at 30 September 2026.

latest_circulars.title: Draft Amendment Directions on "Preventive Safeguards for EBTs": a consultation due 14 December, and no NBFC is in its scope
latest_circulars.summary: The RBI issued for public comment on 23 November 2026 a set of draft Amendment Directions on "Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)" — press release 2026-2027/1548, dated 23 November 2026 and signed by Brij Raj, Chief General Manager. It is a draft issued for comments, with feedback due by 14 December 2026; it is not a rule in force, and no rule changed when it appeared.
latest_circulars.impact: none — the scope is banks and co-operative banks. Nothing in the draft touches the company's gold-loan, funding or securitisation rules, and the comment deadline is a banks' consultation to watch rather than a company obligation.
